exam.description: Comprehensive practical mock containing spotter pins, histology slides, clinical vignettes, and missing asset recovery demonstrations.
exam.instructions: Rotate stations when the OSPE bell rings. Enter identification keys or select multiple choice responses.

questions.title: Station 01: Vascular Operative Anatomy
questions.questionText: Identify the major arterial trunk indicated by Pointer A.
questions.explanation: The celiac trunk arises from the ventral abdominal aorta at the level of T12 immediately below the diaphragmatic aortic hiatus.

questions.title: Station 02: Endocrine Histopathology
questions.questionText: Examine this thyroid FNA biopsy. What classic nuclear feature defines this neoplasm?

options.text: Orphan Annie eye ground-glass nuclei and nuclear pseudoinclusions
Amyloid stroma staining positive with Congo red
Pleomorphic spindle cells with frequent atypical mitoses
Abundant Hurthle cells with granular eosinophilic cytoplasm

questions.explanation: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is characteristically identified by optically clear ground-glass nuclei (Orphan Annie eyes) and psammoma bodies.

questions.title: Station 03: Surgical Triage
questions.clinicalVignette: A 24-year-old male presents with 14 hours of migratory periumbilical pain shifting to the right lower quadrant, low-grade pyrexia (38.1°C), and focal peritonism at McBurney's point. Alvarado score is 8.
questions.questionText: What is the most definitive immediate operative intervention?

options.text: Right hemicolectomy with primary ileocolic anastomosis
Diagnostic colonoscopy and broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
Percutaneous catheter drainage under ultrasound guidance

questions.explanation: An Alvarado score >=7 in a young adult male with clear peritoneal signs in the right iliac fossa warrants prompt surgical appendectomy.

questions.title: Station 04: Surgical Principles
questions.questionText: During a Lichtenstein tension-free inguinal hernia repair, which nerve running on the anterior surface of the spermatic cord is at highest risk of entrapment?
questions.explanation: The ilioinguinal nerve travels through the superficial inguinal ring directly overlying the cord; inadvertent suture fixation leads to chronic postoperative neuralgia.
